JITEngine is a collection of LLM serving engines that [SkyDiscover](https://skydiscover-ai.github.io/) builds on the
fly for specific AI models and hardware (Apple silicon Macs in this case). The six engines featured here decode up to
2.72 times faster than the best alternative server tested on the exact same Mac.

## Quick start

Install the build for your Mac's chip and memory (the one that measured faster on our two Macs) with its model,
then serve it, or run a coding agent on it:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://jitengine.ai/install.sh | bash -s -- flint    # or qwen3.6, flash-next
jitengine start      # serve it on port 8080, in the background
jitengine claude     # or run a coding agent on it: claude, codex, opencode or pi
```

The engine serves the OpenAI and Anthropic APIs:

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions \
  --json '{"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}]}'
```

[jitengine.ai](https://jitengine.ai) gives the commands for your Mac and model, with the speeds we measured on our
two Macs.

<details>
<summary>More install details: disk, memory, <code>sudo</code>, and installing by hand</summary>

Flash-Next needs about 220 GB free on the internal SSD (290 GB for the M4 Pro build with its optional pack16 file)
and builds its expert packs once. `jitengine status`, `logs`, `restart` and `stop` manage the engine, and
`jitengine serve` runs it in the terminal instead.

If less memory is free than the engine's default budget, `jitengine` starts it with the largest budget that fits; the
engine then reads more experts from the SSD and runs slower, and in our tests the output stayed the same. Set
`JITENGINE_BUDGET_GIB` to choose the budget yourself. For Flint on a 24 to 36 GB Mac and Qwen3.6 on a 32 or 36 GB
Mac, `jitengine` asks for `sudo` to raise the GPU's wired memory limit until the Mac restarts.

Each engine's README has the steps to install it by hand, with Python 3.14.

</details>

## Engines

| Engine | Mac | Key idea | Speedup |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| [**Qwen3.6‑35B‑A3B**](engines/qwen3.6-35b-a3b-m2) 3‑bit | 24&nbsp;GB&nbsp;M2 | Its own exact 3-bit GPU kernels | **1.36×** vs llama.cpp + MTP |
| [**Qwen3.6‑35B‑A3B**](engines/qwen3.6-35b-a3b-m4pro) 4‑bit | 48&nbsp;GB&nbsp;M4&nbsp;Pro | Speculative decoding, exact by default | **1.10×** vs oMLX, 8 agents |
| [**Qwen3.8‑Flash‑Next**](engines/qwen3.8-flash-next-m4pro) | 48&nbsp;GB&nbsp;M4&nbsp;Pro | Hot experts in memory, lossless MTP | **2.72×** vs slotstream |
| [**Qwen3.8‑Flash‑Next**](engines/qwen3.8-flash-next-m2) | 24&nbsp;GB&nbsp;M2 | Evicts the experts needed last | **1.62×** vs slotstream |
| [**Flint**](engines/flint-m4pro) int4 | 48&nbsp;GB&nbsp;M4&nbsp;Pro | One KV read for all heads | **1.22×** vs rec, 252K context |
| [**Flint**](engines/flint-m2) int4 | 24&nbsp;GB&nbsp;M2 | SSD streaming, GPU clock held high | **2.1×** vs llama.cpp, raw decode at 1K |

Speedups are for one user unless the row says otherwise. We ran both builds of each model on both Macs;
[`engines/`](engines) says how the two builds differ and which one `install.sh` picks for each chip and memory size.

## Use it with a coding agent

<p align="center">
  <picture>
    <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="assets/jitengine-race-dark.gif">
    <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: light)" srcset="assets/jitengine-race-light.gif">
    <img src="assets/jitengine-race-light.gif" width="100%" alt="Flash-Next on a 48 GB M4 Pro: the same 161-token reply, the engine's own streamed tokens, replayed at each server's measured one-user decode speed. JITEngine at 32.9 tok/s finishes in 4.9 s; slotstream at 12.1 tok/s takes 13.3 s.">
  </picture>
</p>

```bash
jitengine claude      # Claude Code
jitengine codex       # Codex
jitengine opencode    # OpenCode
jitengine pi          # Pi
```

Each command starts the engine if it is not running, then the agent on the local model for that session only; nothing
is written to the agent's config. Install the agent itself first: [Claude Code](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code),
[Codex](https://github.com/openai/codex), [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) or [Pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi).

For another agent, set `http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1` as its OpenAI base URL or `http://127.0.0.1:8080` as its Anthropic
one; both APIs serve tool calls. [`launch/`](launch) has each agent's setup by hand, `jit-launch` for an engine
installed without the one-liner, and the serve flags agents need, such as Qwen3.6's `--max-context 32768`.

## How they were built

In SkyDiscover, coding agents edit the engine, run tests, and benchmark each build against the current best in the
same session. SkyDiscover keeps a build only when it passes every check and wins that head-to-head benchmark by a clear
margin. In the Flash-Next run on the M4 Pro, every kept build produced output bit-identical to the first. In some runs, a separate auditor agent hunted for benchmark cheats; it found none, and turned the coverage
gaps it uncovered into new tests. [Flash-Next on the M4 Pro](engines/qwen3.8-flash-next-m4pro/DETAILS.md#why-its-fast-in-more-detail)
shows one run build by build, and each engine's README explains what made it fast.
